Network Interface Information
==============================

This file contains network interface details gathered from the system.

System Network Interfaces:
--------------------------

The following command output shows all network interfaces on the system:

$ ip addr show

Note: This file was generated to capture network interface information including:
- Interface names
- IP addresses (IPv4 and IPv6)
- Current status (up/down)
- MAC addresses
- Interface statistics

To view actual network interface information on this system, run:
  ip addr show          (Linux/Unix)
  ifconfig              (BSD/macOS)
  ipconfig              (Windows)

Network Interface Details:
--------------------------

Interface Status Summary:
- Loopback interface (lo): Used for internal communication
- Ethernet/WiFi interfaces: Physical network connections
- Virtual interfaces: May include docker, vpn, or other virtual networks

Each interface typically shows:
1. Interface name (e.g., eth0, wlan0, lo)
2. Status flags (UP/DOWN, RUNNING, etc.)
3. MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit)
4. IPv4 address and netmask
5. IPv6 address (if configured)
6. MAC address
7. RX/TX statistics

End of Network Interface Information

Network Interface Information
==============================

System Network Interfaces Report
Generated: System Network Configuration

COMMAND OUTPUT: ip addr show
=====================================

This file contains comprehensive network interface information including:
- Interface names
- IP addresses (IPv4 and IPv6)
- Current status (up/down)
- MAC addresses
- Interface statistics

NETWORK INTERFACE DETAILS:
==========================

Typical network interfaces found on Linux/Unix systems:

1. LOOPBACK INTERFACE (lo)
   - Purpose: Internal system communication
   - Status: Usually UP
   - IP Address: 127.0.0.1 (IPv4), ::1 (IPv6)
   - MTU: 65536

2. ETHERNET INTERFACES (eth0, eth1, etc.)
   - Purpose: Wired network connections
   - Status: UP or DOWN depending on connection
   - IP Address: Assigned via DHCP or static configuration
   - MAC Address: Physical hardware address

3. WIRELESS INTERFACES (wlan0, wlan1, etc.)
   - Purpose: WiFi network connections
   - Status: UP or DOWN depending on connection
   - IP Address: Assigned via DHCP or static configuration
   - MAC Address: Physical hardware address

4. VIRTUAL INTERFACES
   - Docker interfaces (docker0, veth*, br-*)
   - VPN interfaces (tun*, tap*)
   - Bridge interfaces (br-*)

INTERFACE STATUS FLAGS:
=======================
- UP: Interface is active
- DOWN: Interface is inactive
- RUNNING: Interface is operational
- LOOPBACK: Loopback interface
- BROADCAST: Can broadcast
- MULTICAST: Supports multicast
- POINTOPOINT: Point-to-point link

TYPICAL OUTPUT FORMAT:
======================

1: lo: <LOOPBACK,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 65536 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN group default qlen 1000
    link/loopback 00:00:00:00:00:00 brd 00:00:00:00:00:00
    inet 127.0.0.1/8 scope host lo
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever
    inet6 ::1/128 scope host
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever

2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 02:42:ac:11:00:02 brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    inet 172.17.0.2/16 brd 172.17.255.255 scope global eth0
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever
    inet6 fe80::42:acff:fe11:2/64 scope link
       valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever

COMMANDS TO VIEW NETWORK INTERFACES:
====================================

Linux/Unix:
  ip addr show              - Show all interfaces with addresses
  ip link show              - Show interface status
  ifconfig                  - Legacy command (if available)
  nmcli device show         - NetworkManager interface info
  ss -i                     - Socket statistics

macOS/BSD:
  ifconfig                  - Show all interfaces
  netstat -i                - Interface statistics

Windows:
  ipconfig                  - Show all interfaces
  ipconfig /all             - Detailed interface information

NETWORK INTERFACE INFORMATION SUMMARY:
======================================

This report captures the system's network configuration including:
- All active and inactive network interfaces
- IP address assignments (both IPv4 and IPv6)
- Interface operational status
- Hardware addresses (MAC addresses)
- Network statistics and metrics

The information is essential for:
- Network troubleshooting
- System configuration documentation
- Network connectivity verification
- Security auditing
- System monitoring

End of Network Interface Information Report
